policy_title: Improve NHS efficiency and cut waste
stated: Reform UK will improve NHS efficiency by opening operating theatres on weekends, planning rotas further in advance, negotiating better procurement prices, reviewing Private Finance Contracts, charging those who fail to attend appointments without notice, and abolishing the NHS Race and Health Observatory.

source.quote: Improve Efficiency. Cut Waste and Unnecessary Managers Operating theatres must be open on weekends. Rotas must be planned further in advance. Nail down better prices using economies of scale. Review all NHS Private Finance Contracts for significant savings potential. Charge those who fail to attend medical appointments without notice. Abolish the NHS Race and Health Observatory.

bearing_set.reason: Weekend theatre openings, advanced rota planning, procurement savings, and no-show charging all directly affect NHS throughput, waiting times, and appointment access — the core O3 indicators.

Abolishing the NHS Race and Health Observatory removes the dedicated institutional mechanism for monitoring and addressing racial health disparities, bearing concretely on minority protections and equal treatment in healthcare access.
Reviewing Private Finance Initiative contracts and negotiating procurement prices are explicit fiscal measures that affect the NHS cost base and the funded/borrowed balance of public health spending.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the main efficiency cluster lands on O3; the Observatory abolition earns a real O9 verdict on minority/equal-treatment grounds; PFI and procurement measures have direct public-finance implications (O12). The no-show charge is a behavioural deterrent too narrow and uncertain in scale to earn standalone O11 or O2 verdicts.
